governing_table.code: No statewide building or plumbing code for all buildings. State law makes the International Building Code (one of the last three editions adopted by the Mississippi Building Codes Council) the State Uniform Construction Code that counties and cities adopt, and counties and cities could opt out. The table in that model code is IBC Table 2902.1 (the same table as International Plumbing Code Table 403.1).
governing_table.edition: Varies by city or county. Text read: 2024 IBC, the edition the State Fire Marshal adopted as of July 1, 2024 for state-owned buildings, public assembly buildings and buildings 75 feet or taller; rows also compared with the 2018 IBC.
governing_table.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 2902.1 based on the actual use of the building or space. Uses not shown in Table 2902.1 shall be considered individually by the code official. The number of occupants shall be determined by this code.
governing_table.scope_note: Miss. Code 17-2-4 (read on FindLaw, current as of January 1, 2025): a county board of supervisors or municipal governing authority 'shall adopt and amend as minimum codes one (1) of the following as the State Uniform Construction Code', including 'One (1) of the last three (3) adopted editions of the International Building Code (IBC)' and other codes covering electrical, plumbing, mechanical, fire and fuel gas; within 120 days of the section taking effect a county or municipality could choose 'not to be subject to the code requirements imposed under this section'. The statute names no plumbing code or edition. Which editions the Mississippi Building Codes Council has adopted could not be read on any council page (apps.mid.ms.gov/ubc/ubc.aspx returns 404).
governing_table.adoption_quote: AS OF JULY 1, 2024, THE STATE OF MISSISSIPPI - OFFICE OF THE STATE FIRE MARSHAL HAS ADOPTED THE 2024 ADDITION OF THE INTERNATIONAL FIRE CODE (IFC) AND THE INTERNATIONAL BUILDING CODE (IBC).
governing_table.amendments: No state amendments to IBC Chapter 29 found. UpCodes labels 'Mississippi Building Code 2024' as 'Adopts Without Amendments' and says building codes in Mississippi are adopted and governed at the local level.
governing_table.edition_differences: 2018 IBC as read on UpCodes: office, restaurant and school rows are the same as 2024 (1 per 25 for the first 50 then 1 per 50; 1 per 75; 1 per 50). The 2018 edition has no exception allowing shared all-gender rooms and says single-user rooms 'shall be identified for use by either sex'. The 2021 edition was not hosted for Mississippi and was not read.

office.row_label: 2 Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, nonmedical professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: See IPC Section 424.2 (may replace up to 50% of the required men's water closets)
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.urinals: See IPC Section 424.2 (may replace up to 67% of the required men's water closets)
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts d | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200 | - | 1 per 500 | 1 service sink

school.urinals: See IPC Section 424.2 (may replace up to 67% of the required men's water closets)
school.quote: Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | 1 per 50 | - | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink

sex_split.text: Total occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistics show a different split.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exceptions: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number, for each sex.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required men's toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational buildings and up to 50% elsewhere. Each urinal needs a privacy partition. Read on a copy of the 2024 International Plumbing Code hosted for Georgia, because UpCodes hosts no plumbing code for Mississippi.
urinal_substitution.quote: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in all other occupancies.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load is 15 or fewer, in business occupancies of 25 or fewer, or in mercantile occupancies of 100 or fewer.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: IBC Table 1004.5: business areas 150 gross sq ft per occupant; assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; educational classroom area 20 net.
occupant_load.quote: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net ... Business areas | 150 gross ... Classroom area | 20 net

stall_required.text: Each toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door; each urinal needs partitions.
stall_required.quote: Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. | Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 1 = 0.5, so none.
50 women, 50 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 50/25 = 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 2 = 1, so 1.
100 women, 100 men. First 50: 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50: 1; total 3 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 women, 200 men. First 50: 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50: 3; total 5 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25/75 = 0.33, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/75 = 0.67, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 each. 25/50 = 0.5, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/50 = 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
100 each. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals may replace up to 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Worked on the model IBC table, which applies only where the city or county has adopted it unamended. The urinal limit applies 'in each bathroom or toilet room'; the figures assume one men's room holds all the men's fixtures.

hdpe_fire.section: IBC Section 803.9 (with 803.1.1 and the Chapter 2 definition of interior wall and ceiling finish), 2024 and 2018 editions; the same sentence is 2024 International Fire Code Section 803.9. Not a statewide rule for all buildings: it applies where the State Fire Marshal's code applies (state-owned buildings, public assembly buildings and buildings 75 feet or taller, unless the county or city has its own fire code) and wherever a city or county has adopted the 2018 or later IBC.
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | Chapter 2, Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish: The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; ...
hdpe_fire.note: Code sections read on UpCodes (secondary). Adoption read on the State Fire Marshal's page and in the Rules and Regulations for the Mississippi Fire Prevention Code (19 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 7, Ch. 7, effective January 1, 2025): 'The Mississippi Fire Prevention Code adopts the International Fire Code ... up to and including the most current edition ... To the extent the International Building Code (IBC) and the International Residential Code (IRC) apply or impact application of the International Fire Code (IFC), the most recent and current version shall be utilized.' and 'Any county or municipality may adopt a fire prevention code with standards not less stringent than the Mississippi Fire Prevention Code'.

access.state_standard: No separate modern state accessibility code. Where a city or county has adopted the IBC, Chapter 11 requires ICC A117.1 (the 2024 IBC references ICC A117.1-2017 with Supplement 1; the edition depends on the IBC edition adopted locally). The federal 2010 ADA Standards apply everywhere. An older state law, Miss. Code 43-6-101 to 43-6-125, sets its own specifications for buildings paid for with public funds.

differences.point: Toe clearance under stall partitions (wheelchair stall)
differences.state: A117.1-2017 604.9.5.1: 12 inches high and 8 inches beyond the partition; not needed at the front if the stall is deeper than 64 inches (wall-hung toilet) or 67 inches (floor-mounted), nor at the side if wider than 68 inches.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.8.1.4: 'a toe clearance of 9 inches (230 mm) minimum above the finish floor and 6 inches (150 mm) deep minimum beyond the compartment-side face of the partition'; exception above 62 or 65 inches deep and 66 inches wide.
differences.quote: The front partition and at least one side partition of wheelchair accessible toilet compartments shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the floor and extending 8 inches (205 mm) beyond the compartment side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members.

differences.point: Vertical grab bar on the side wall
differences.state: A117.1-2017 604.5.1 requires a vertical grab bar, 18 inches minimum, in addition to the horizontal side bar; in an ambulatory stall on both sides (604.10.4).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.5.1: 'The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.' No vertical bar.
differences.quote: Fixed side-wall grab bars shall include a horizontal bar complying with Section 604.5.1.1 and a vertical grab bar complying with Section 604.5.1.2. | A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.

differences.point: Wheelchair turning space and the stall
differences.state: A117.1-2017 603.2.1: the turning space may not be inside a toilet compartment.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 603.2.1: 'Turning space complying with 304 shall be provided within the room.' No bar on using the compartment.
differences.quote: A turning space shall be provided within the room. The required turning space shall not be provided within a toilet compartment.

differences.state: IBC 2024 1110.2.1: required in assembly and mercantile occupancies where six or more toilets are required in total.
differences.federal: No such requirement in the 2010 ADA Standards sections 213 and 604 (213.3.1 covers only wheelchair and ambulatory compartments).
differences.quote: In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required.

differences.state: Miss. Code 43-6-113 (buildings of assembly, schools, offices and other public buildings built with state, county or municipal funds): each sex's toilet room needs at least one stall 3 feet wide, at least 4 feet 8 inches deep, with a 32-inch door that swings out, handrails on each side 33 inches high, and a seat 20 inches from the floor.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.8.1 wheelchair compartment (60 inches wide minimum), 604.5 grab bars on the side wall closest to the toilet and on the rear wall. The state specification is older and mostly less demanding; handrails on each side and the 20-inch seat differ from the federal standard.
differences.quote: Toilet rooms for each sex shall have at least one (1) toilet stall that: (a) is three (3) feet wide; (b) is at least four (4) feet eight (8) inches, preferably five (5) feet deep; (c) has a door (where doors are used) that is thirty-two (32) inches wide and swings out; (d) has handrails on each side, thirty-three (33) inches high and parallel to the floor ... (e) has a water closet with the seat twenty (20) inches from the floor.

access.same_as_federal: Number of stalls: IBC 2024 1110.2.4 and ADA 213.3.1 both require a wheelchair stall wherever stalls are provided and an ambulatory stall where the room has six or more stalls, or six or more toilets and urinals combined. Ambulatory stall 35 to 37 inches wide, 60 deep in both. Children's stall sizes and door signs were not compared.
access.process: No state registration or plan-review step for accessibility was found for private commercial projects. For buildings built with public funds, Miss. Code 43-6-123 makes the State Board of Health 'responsible for reviewing plans and specifications' for compliance with the 1972 specifications, for a fee of 'one-half of one percent (1/2 of 1%) of the estimated cost, with a maximum fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00)'. Whether the Board still runs this review was not confirmed. The State Fire Marshal reviews plans for fire code compliance on request and for state buildings (plan review, 601-359-1061).

single_user.rule: No Mississippi statute on signs for single-user restrooms was found. Where a city or county has adopted the 2021 or 2024 IBC, single-user rooms count toward the required fixtures and must be identified as available to everyone regardless of sex (2018 edition: 'identified for use by either sex'). In public education buildings the SAFER Act treats a 'single-sex or family-use restroom' (one occupant or a family, floor-to-ceiling walls, full door with a secure lock) as an alternative to male and female rooms.
single_user.quote: Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.

all_gender_shared.rule: The 2024 IBC allows a shared room for all persons where every toilet is in a compartment with a door and urinals have privacy partitions; the fixture count is then worked out on the total occupant load. The 2018 IBC has no such exception, so in a city on the 2018 edition separate rooms are required unless a small-occupancy exception applies. In public schools, public universities and community colleges, state law requires multi-user restrooms designated for females and for males, or single-occupant rooms.
all_gender_shared.quote: Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the International Plumbing Code and for urinals in accordance with Section 405.3.5 of the International Plumbing Code. | Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load.

use_restrictions.rule: SAFER Act (Senate Bill 2753, 2024 Regular Session; Miss. Code 29-18-1 to 29-18-19; approved by the Governor May 13, 2024, effective on passage). Applies to public education buildings: any building owned, operated, rented or leased by or to a public school, public university, public community or junior college or the institutions of higher learning. Such a building that has a restroom must have a female and a male restroom, or a single-sex or family-use restroom, and a person may not enter a restroom designated for the opposite sex except in listed cases. No statute was found covering private buildings or city and county buildings generally.
use_restrictions.quote: Any public education building that maintains a restroom shall, at a minimum, have: (a) A restroom designated for exclusive use by females and a restroom designated for exclusive use by males; or (b) A single-sex or family-use restroom. | "Restroom" means a space designated for multiple individuals that includes toilets and/or urinals. | "Single-sex or family-use restroom" means a room that includes a toilet or urinal and that is intended for a single occupant or a family, is enclosed by floor-to-ceiling walls, and is accessed by a full door with a secure lock that prevents another individual from entering while the room is in use. | For purposes of this act, a person may not enter a restroom, changing facility, or single-sex educational housing space, designated for the opposite sex, except under the following circumstances
use_restrictions.note: Read as the bill 'As Sent to Governor' on the Legislature's site, with the bill history showing '05/13 Approved by Governor'. The codified text was not read (the official code site is LexisNexis).

public_wage.law: None. The U.S. Department of Labor lists Mississippi among the states without a prevailing wage law. Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded or assisted construction.
public_wage.quote: States without Prevailing Wage Laws ... Mississippi
public_wage.note: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, 'Dollar Threshold Amount for Contract Coverage' (last revised January 1, 2023), read through the fetch tool. The federal Davis-Bacon threshold and sam.gov rates were not read in this pass. Whether a Mississippi statute bars cities from setting their own wage rules on public jobs was not found.

sales_tax.state_rate_quote: The general tax rate is 7%; however, there are reduced rates for certain sales and there are exemptions provided by law.
sales_tax.local_note: DOR: 'Mississippi has two local tax levies at the city level, and none at the county level. The City of Tupelo levies an additional .25% ... The City of Jackson levies an additional 1% on certain retail sales made from taxpayers within the corporate limits and services provided within the corporate limits. Please review the Notice 72-14-2 for those sales excluded from the 1% Infrastructure tax.' Notice 72-14-2 was not read: the city agent should check whether the Jackson 1% applies to partitions and to out-of-state sellers.

shipped_goods.rule: Goods shipped into Mississippi from out of state are subject to use tax at the sales tax rate (7%). An out-of-state business with more than $250,000 of sales into Mississippi over any twelve months must register and collect. If the seller does not collect, the buyer pays use tax directly to the Department of Revenue.
shipped_goods.quote: Use tax applies to purchases of items that are shipped or delivered into Mississippi from an out-of-state location. ... If you purchase an item from an out-of-state vendor for use in Mississippi and the vendor does not collect the Mississippi sales or use tax, you must pay the use tax directly to the Mississippi Department of Revenue. | The use tax is calculated at the same rate as the sales tax would be if the item is subject to sales tax. | Effective July 1, 2018, businesses located out of the state that have sales into the state of Mississippi that exceed $250,000 over any twelve month period are considered to have substantial economic presence in the state and are required to register with the Mississippi Department of Revenue in order to collect and remit tax.

freight.rule: Shipping, handling and delivery charges on a sale of goods are taxed.
freight.quote: Are transportation, freight or delivery charges in connection with the sale of goods taxable? Yes, tangible personal property is subject to sales tax on the gross proceeds of the sale including, but not limited to, charges for shipping, handling and delivery.

install_labor.rule: Installation labor sold with the goods is taxed. On a commercial construction, renovation or repair contract over $10,000 the 3.5% contractor's tax applies to the whole contract instead (see furnish_and_install). The FAQ does not say how installation labor billed by a separate installer, on a job of $10,000 or less with no sale of goods, is taxed.
install_labor.quote: Is installation labor taxable? Installation labor is taxable when sold in connection with tangible personal property.

furnish_and_install.rule: A 3.5% contractor's tax applies to the total contract price of construction, renovation or repair of non-residential real property when it exceeds $10,000. The tax is on the contractor, not the customer, also on jobs for schools and government. After qualifying the job the contractor gets a Material Purchase Certificate and buys component materials free of sales or use tax. An owner who buys materials directly pays the regular sales tax. The FAQ does not name toilet partitions.
furnish_and_install.quote: Sales Tax Law levies a 3.5% contractor's tax on all construction, renovation or repair of non-residential, real property when the total contract price or compensation received exceeds $10,000. If the contract exceeds $75,000 in scope or if the contractor is from another state, the contractor's tax must be paid before work begins. | A Material Purchase Certificate (MPC) is issued by the Department of Revenue after a contractor has qualified a project. This certificate allows the prime or general contractor and his sub-contractors to purchase component building materials and component services exempt from sales or use tax. | The tax is imposed on the contractor and not on the contractor's customer, regardless of who is the real property owner. | Suppliers that sell to owners who are building their own structures must charge sales tax on materials, supplies, and equipment sold or rented to property owners. Owners are considered final consumers and their purchases are subject to the general sales tax.

sales_tax.note: All from the Department's Sales Tax Frequently Asked Questions page, which says it is general information and that the Mississippi Code and Administrative Code govern. The statute (Miss. Code 27-65-21) and the Department's Guide for Construction Contractors were not read.

page.stalls_intro: Mississippi has no single statewide building code: each city or county adopts its own edition of the model building rules, and state law names that model as the standard. The model counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and fractions round up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to two thirds of the toilets in a restaurant or school and up to half in an office, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: These figures come from the model rules, so confirm the count with the local building department, which can also say which edition applies. These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the model rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** the building and fire rules the State Fire Marshal applies to state-owned buildings, public assembly buildings and buildings 75 feet or taller require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. The model rules most cities adopt say the same. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law sets the sizes everywhere. Mississippi has no separate modern state access code, and where a city has adopted the model building rules, their access standard applies too.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Mississippi extras:** the access standard in the newest model building rules asks for more than the federal one in a wheelchair stall: 12 inches of toe space under the partitions instead of 9, and an upright grab bar on the side wall as well as the horizontal one. An older state law also sets stall sizes for buildings paid for with public money and has the State Board of Health review the plans. Ask the local building department which standard it enforces.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under the newest model building rules a one-person restroom is marked as open to everyone, and a shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals have privacy screens. Older editions don't allow the shared room, so ask the local building department. Mississippi law requires public schools, community colleges and public universities to have restrooms designated for females and for males, or one-person rooms.
page.public_jobs: Mississippi has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on federally funded work.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Mississippi, installation labor sold together with the partitions is taxed. On a commercial construction or renovation contract above $10,000, the contractor instead pays a 3.5% contractor's tax on the whole contract price and buys the materials free of sales tax.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable at the state rate of 7%, freight included. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Mississippi Department of Revenue

page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2017 as referenced by the 2024 International Building Code (edition depends on local adoption); International Building Code (2024 edition adopted by the State Fire Marshal from July 1, 2024; local editions vary) and Mississippi Fire Prevention Code (2024 International Fire Code); International Plumbing Code where adopted locally; Mississippi Code Sections 17-2-4, 43-6-101 to 43-6-125 and 29-18-1 to 29-18-19; NFPA 286 for HDPE.

The Jackson 1% special sales tax (DOR Notice 72-14-2) is a city item.
